feedback.problem:
The vector $v$ in the plane is mapped to the vector $[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ whose matrix $T$ is given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the original vector $v?$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the given information, we have 

$$
T\cdot v=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to calculate the inverse of $T$, which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-(-8)}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the original vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{7}{10}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
